key_concepts: Cellular respiration breaks down glucose to release energy as ATP
The main stages are glycolysis, Krebs cycle, and electron transport chain
Most stages of cellular respiration occur in the mitochondrion
Raw materials are glucose and oxygen; end products are carbon dioxide and water
Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm and splits glucose into two pyruvate molecules
Glycolysis yields a net gain of 2 ATP and 2 NADH
Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix and oxidizes pyruvate/acetyl-CoA to carbon
Krebs cycle produces ATP, NADH, and FADH2
The electron transport chain is embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane and produces
The electron transport chain yields about 3 ATP per NADH and 2 ATP per FADH2
Oxygen is the final electron acceptor in the electron transport chain and forms water
